studies.label: Marketing-campaign experiment (generic vs personalized vs partially personalized GPT-4o assistant)

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 19, Participants; confirmed by PDF p. 52 (printed supplement p. 24), Table S2
counts_source.quote: After applying these exclusion criteria, a sample of 331 individuals was brought forward for analysis with 116 participants randomized to generic AI, 114 to personalized AI, and 101 to partially personalized AI (Table S2).

arms.name: Generic AI
arms.description: GPT-4o assistant with company context and an initial campaign idea, prompted to ask focused questions, build on contributions, and give feedback; receives no personal profile. PDF pp. 21-22; PDF p. 37 (printed supplement p. 9).

arms.name: Personalized AI
arms.description: Same assistant plus the participant’s synthesized demographic, cognitive, psychological, and creativity profile and their AI-guided interview summary about marketing experience and work style. PDF pp. 21-22; PDF p. 38 (printed supplement p. 10).

arms.name: Partially personalized AI
arms.description: Same personalized configuration, supplied with another participant’s profile and interview summary. PDF p. 22.

studies.task: Develop a marketing-campaign plan for Cultivated, a fictional lab-grown ribeye startup, addressing positioning, audience, messaging and trust, channels and experiences, and success metrics while using the assigned assistant.

ai_tool.name: GPT-4o (temperature = 1), with custom generic or personalized system prompts
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 21, Experimental Design; model also cited as Hurst et al. (2024), GPT-4o system card, reference 83 on PDF p. 27.

preregistration.where: PDF p. 19 says “We re-registered our study design and primary analyses” and links to https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/QF3G7. The citation record identifies an original registration and an amendment, but the saved manuscript does not establish prospective timing or its prespecified outcome hierarchy. Attempts to check the named OSF registration and amended-response APIs were blocked by network permissions.

estimates.outcome: Campaign quality, expert-human pairwise Elo (random validation sample)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Expert Prolific raters working in management, consulting, or market research made blind pairwise choices of overall campaign quality. A final Elo score was estimated per campaign. Only a randomly selected validation sample from the Generic AI and Personalized AI arms was rated (PDF p. 32, printed supplement p. 4).

regression.model: Reported treatment coefficient for expert-human campaign Elo. The same paragraph reports a marketing-skills coefficient, but does not give the full model formula or covariate list.

sources.locator: PDF p. 32 (printed supplement p. 4), Sensitivity Analyses, expert-human validation
sources.quote: We randomly selected a subset of 100 marketing campaigns, restricting our comparison to only generic or personalized AI.

sources.locator: PDF p. 32 (printed supplement p. 4), Sensitivity Analyses, expert-human validation
sources.quote: We find that there is no significant difference between treatment conditions (β = 158.2, p = 0.14)

estimates.notes: Includes all campaigns measured in the random validation sample, rather than a quality- or skill-defined subgroup. Each campaign is one participant’s submitted output; the analyzed score is the final campaign Elo, not each individual rating. The printed sample size counts campaigns, so n_units is recorded and person-count fields remain null; arm-specific validation counts are not printed. Full-experiment arm sizes must not be substituted. The regression covariates are incompletely reported: unlike the LLM Elo caption, this paragraph does not explicitly state adjustment for post-treatment turn count. If the human validation model also adjusts for turn count, this estimate must be excluded under extraction rule 5; this is an open item. No SE, arm means, arm SDs, or standardized treatment effect are printed. Higher Elo means better campaign quality (usefulness).

estimates.outcome: Campaign theme diversity relative to the pooled campaign centroid (paper: creativity)
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: GPT-4o extracts distinctive campaign themes; text-embedding-3-large embeds them. Each submitted campaign is compared with the mean embedding of all campaigns across treatment conditions (PDF p. 23). Although Methods calls the operation cosine similarity, Results explicitly interprets higher printed creativity scores as less homogeneity (PDF p. 10). The transformation to the reported scale is not specified.

estimates.notes: Full-sample arm summaries, separate from the quality-tertile analyses. This measure compares participants with a common centroid pooled across conditions; it is not within-arm dispersion. Both arm means and both arm CIs are retained without subtraction, sign reversal, rescaling, or conversion to an SE. The standard ci_* fields describe the treatment mean; additional control_ci_* fields preserve the Generic AI mean’s printed CI. Neither interval is a CI for the between-arm difference. No full-sample pairwise coefficient, test, p-value, arm SD, or contrast SE is printed. The CI construction and treatment of dependence through the shared centroid are not reported, hence se_basis is unclear. The paper does not state whether AI-only benchmark campaigns enter the centroid. n_total and n_units are null because no two-arm analysis total is printed; arm counts come from the complete analyzed sample in Table S2.

estimates.outcome: Percentage of final-campaign words differing from the AI-recommended campaign
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Reported percentage of words different between the submitted campaign and the campaign recommended by that participant’s AI assistant. The word-matching algorithm, denominator, and aggregation method are not specified (PDF pp. 50-51, printed supplement pp. 22-23).

sources.locator: PDF p. 51 (printed supplement p. 23), Personalization Shifted Conversations from Collaborative to Strategic
sources.quote: Approximately 80.5% of words were different between the final campaign and what their AI assistant recommended versus 64.5% in the personalized arm.

estimates.notes: The preceding paragraph identifies Generic AI users as the comparison group (PDF p. 50). The paper reports a condition comparison without a stated subgroup restriction; it does not print analysis counts. The mean fields retain the reported arm percentages in percent units, including the approximate wording in the source; no conversion to proportions is made. It is not stated whether these are means of per-campaign percentages or percentages pooled over words, so unit and counts are null. Higher values mean more editing or divergence from one’s own AI draft, with no established favorable creativity direction. This is other/with_ai, not across_people, because the comparison is against the same participant’s AI draft rather than other people’s outputs. No uncertainty or test is reported. This output-scored measure is absent from the screening outcome list, so form_outcome_id is null.

open_items: Pre-exclusion randomized counts and exclusions by arm are not printed. PDF p. 19 distinguishes recruitment from the retained analysis sample; do not treat recruitment or post-exclusion counts as allocation totals.

Unadjusted full-sample campaign-quality treatment effects and arm means/SDs are absent. The main LLM quality, alternative-scoring, and LLM Elo models control post-treatment messages/turns and are excluded.

The full expert-human Elo regression specification is not printed. Verify whether it adjusts for post-treatment turn count, as the LLM models do; if so, exclude the retained validation record. Human-rating arm counts, participant analysis count, SE, and arm SDs are also unreported.

The diversity-score transformation, CI construction, handling of the common centroid, and inclusion of autonomous AI campaigns in that centroid are unspecified. Full-sample human AI-arm pairwise tests or contrast SEs are not printed.
Campaign-length regressions have no stated full model specification, SE, or arm SDs. The overall length SD pools every arm and must not be mislabeled as a control-arm or two-arm pooled SD.
For the percentage of final words differing from the AI draft, the comparison algorithm, denominator, aggregation level, analysis counts, and uncertainty are not reported.

The manuscript does not establish registration timing relative to data collection or a prespecified primary-outcome hierarchy. The supplied citation record establishes an associated registration and amendment, but the named OSF APIs could not be independently accessed during this extraction.
The excluded personalized LLM Elo result has discrepant printed p-values in the narrative and figure caption. The record does not select one or create a duplicate estimate.
notes: Extraction B, checked against the local PDF on 2026-10-11. Read the complete markdown conversion in contiguous chunks, including the appendices; inspected PDF tables and figures and checked each retained number directly in PDF text. All recorded statistics are transcribed, with no computed differences, SEs, standardized effects, counts, or figure digitization. One randomized human experiment is retained; the model-only benchmark is listed in not_extracted. No unassisted arm or after-AI outcome is reported. No cross-paper sample overlap is stated. PDF p. 19 supplies the detailed recruitment/exclusion flow despite the shorter recruitment description on PDF p. 18. Human expert validation uses a random measurement subsample and is retained separately with unresolved adjustment status flagged. Two additional control_ci_* endpoints and a control_ci_level field are used for diversity records to preserve the printed control-arm uncertainty without mislabeling it as contrast uncertainty. The current codebook maps ordinary word count to length, resolving the older screening form’s vocabulary gap. The final-output editing measure is an additional output-scored other outcome and is not pooled as creativity or diversity.
